walkthrough.getStarted.title: Get started with Codex Terminal
walkthrough.getStarted.description: Install Codex, launch a native terminal session, choose a profile, and find your conversations in History.
walkthrough.install.title: Install the Codex CLI
walkthrough.install.description: Install Codex with `npm install -g @openai/codex`, or set `codexTerminal.command` to an executable path. Then run [Codex Terminal: Doctor](command:codexTerminal.doctor) to verify it.
walkthrough.launch.title: Launch your first session
walkthrough.launch.description: Open the Codex Terminal activity-bar view and run [New Session](command:codexTerminal.new). A native terminal tab opens in the workspace.
walkthrough.profile.title: Choose the Codex terminal profile
walkthrough.profile.description: Use the terminal `+` dropdown and choose **Codex**, or run [New Session with Profile](command:codexTerminal.newWithProfile) to select a saved profile.
walkthrough.history.title: Find conversations in History
walkthrough.history.description: Open the History view in the Codex Terminal activity bar. It reads Codex's local session store and lets you resume, export, archive, or delete conversations. Use [Refresh Codex History](command:codexTerminal.refreshHistory) after changing the store.

capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces.descrip: Codex Terminal launches a shell, so the settings that name the program, its arguments, or its environment are ignored in an untrusted workspace. Trust the folder to use workspace-level values for them.
capabilities.virtualWorkspaces.descripti: Codex Terminal launches a local shell and reads Codex's session files from disk, neither of which exists in a virtual workspace.
configuration.title: Codex Terminal
setting.shell.auto: PowerShell 7 (pwsh) on Windows, falling back to Windows PowerShell; the login shell elsewhere.
setting.shell.editorDefault: Whatever VS Code's default terminal profile is. This is the only mode that types the command into the shell instead of passing it as an argument.
setting.shell.markdownDescription: Shell that hosts Codex. Every mode except `editorDefault` passes the command as a shell argument, so nothing is typed into the prompt and the launch cannot race shell startup.
setting.customShellPath.description: Absolute path to the shell executable. Used only when codexTerminal.shell is 'custom'.
setting.command.description: Codex CLI command or absolute path to its executable. Paths containing spaces are quoted for you.
setting.args.description: Extra arguments appended to every Codex launch, for example ["--model", "gpt-5.1-codex"].
setting.keepShellOpen.description: Stay at a live shell prompt after Codex exits instead of closing the tab.
setting.location.editor: A tab in the editor area, next to your file tabs.
setting.location.editorBeside: A tab in the editor area, split beside the active editor.
setting.reuseTerminal.description: Focus the existing Codex terminal instead of opening a new tab.
setting.cwd.activeFileFolder: The directory containing the active file.
setting.cwd.activeFileWorkspaceFolder: The workspace folder containing the active file, falling back to the first workspace folder.
setting.cwd.prompt: Prompt when a multi-root workspace has no active file to disambiguate the folder.
setting.env.description: Environment variables added to the Codex terminal.
setting.terminalName.description: Name shown on the terminal tab. Used when codexTerminal.tabTitle is 'static', and as the marker that identifies Codex tabs after a window reload.
setting.tabTitle.live: Let Codex drive the tab title, so the activity spinner animates while it works.
setting.tabTitle.static: Show a fixed 'project — Codex' label. The tab cannot animate in this mode.
setting.tabTitle.markdownDescription:
Who owns the terminal tab title.

`live` leaves the name unset so the editor subscribes to the title Codex emits, which is what makes the tab show a spinner while a turn runs. Supplying a name makes the editor skip that subscription entirely, so `static` tabs never animate.
setting.iconColor.description: Theme color id used to tint the tab icon. Empty string uses the default foreground.
setting.showStatusBarButton.description: Show a Codex button in the status bar.
setting.showStatusBarItem.deprecation: Use codexTerminal.showStatusBarButton; this setting is migrated automatically once per extension version.
setting.showEditorTitleButton.descriptio: Show a Codex button in the editor title bar.
setting.stallSeconds.description: Seconds of silence after which a working Codex session is reported as producing no output. Codex writes nothing to its session file while it waits for an approval and nothing while it is stuck, and the two cannot be told apart from outside, so the elapsed silence is reported rather than a guessed state.
setting.showContextInStatusBar.descripti: Append the highest context usage across live Codex sessions to the status bar item. The session closest to its limit is the one about to force a compaction.
setting.modelRates.description: Your own token prices, keyed by model, used to estimate what a session costs. Empty by default and deliberately not shipped with prices: Codex records internal model aliases such as `gpt-5.6-luna`, and a bundled price list would go stale without ever looking wrong. A key that is a prefix of the recorded model matches it, so `gpt-5.6` prices every `gpt-5.6-*`. A model with no entry shows no cost rather than a zero. Example: `{ "gpt-5.6": { "input": 1.25, "cachedInput": 0.125, "output": 10 } }`
setting.modelRates.cachedInput.descripti: USD per million cached input tokens. Omit to bill cache hits at the full input rate.
setting.modelRates.output.description: USD per million output tokens, reasoning tokens included.
setting.notifyOnCompletion.description: Show a notification when a Codex turn completes. Uses an invocation-scoped notify hook and never edits ~/.codex/config.toml.
setting.titleItems.description: Codex items rendered in the terminal tab title. The default shows a live activity spinner and the project name.
command.askAboutSelection.title: Ask Codex About Selection…
command.revertWorkbenchSettings.title: Revert Workbench Settings
setting.applyWorkbenchSettings.markdownD: Let Codex Terminal set three global `terminal.integrated.*` settings: `tabs.allowAgentCliTitle` and `${sequence}` in `tabs.description` make Codex's live tab title possible; `confirmOnKill` turns close confirmation off for **every terminal in this editor**, not only Codex tabs. Each is written **once**, and once you change one yourself it is never rewritten. *Revert Codex Terminal's Workbench Settings* turns this off, which is what makes the revert survive a window reload.
setting.appServer.enabled.markdownDescri: **Experimental.** Host a `codex app-server` for this window and attach every terminal it launches to it with `--remote`, so Codex reports its own activity over a supported protocol instead of having it inferred from session files. Off by default: the app server is marked experimental by Codex and its protocol carries no compatibility guarantee. Requires a WebSocket-capable editor (VS Code built on Node 22 or newer); if one is unavailable the launch falls back to a plain `codex` and says so in the log.
setting.monitor.enabled.markdownDescript: Read Codex's session files to show live activity, context usage and crash recovery. Turning this off stops all reading of your conversations — and with it the live status **and** the ability to offer interrupted sessions back, because both depend on knowing which conversation a tab belongs to. Launching, resuming and browsing history are unaffected.
setting.journal.storeMessages.markdownDe: Keep Codex's closing message for each turn in the crash-recovery journal, so an interrupted session can be recognised by what it last said. Turning this off keeps conversation text out of the journal; the journal still records identifiers and timestamps, which is all recovery strictly needs.
setting.transcript.includeToolCalls.desc: Include the commands Codex ran and the patches it applied in an exported transcript. Each block is capped, because an apply_patch call carries the entire new contents of every file it writes.
setting.transcript.includeToolOutput.des: Also include what those commands printed back. Off by default: tool output is the bulk of a session and is rarely what you came back to read.
setting.transcript.redactSecrets.descrip: Replace recognised bearer tokens and API-key shapes in exported Markdown, and report the replacement count in its header. On by default; turning this off is a deliberate opt-out and may expose credentials.
setting.history.maxSessions.description: Maximum number of recent Codex sessions shown in the History sidebar.
